newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - German mark not a "village currency".
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - German mark not a "village currency".

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Monday dismissed a recent remark by German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, who warned that the European Union could not compete in world trade if it only had "village currencies".
In a speech to an institute in Freiburg, Tietmeyer did not mention the minister by name, but his remarks were a clear reference to the Kinkel comments made last week.
"It is true that "village currencies' do not always meet the requirements of a globalised economy," Tietmeyer said according to the text of a speech.
"But the mark as the second most important reserve and investment currency should only be viewed as a village currency by a man who views the world as a village anyway," he added.

Arguing for the euro, Kinkel told reporters in Bonn last week that even the mark would be a "village currency" in 10 years compared to the dollar and the Japanese yen because of their dominant role in world trade.

Kinkel admitted his new term -- "Dorfwaehrungen" in German -- was a bit exaggerated but said it had brought the message home to average Germans attending pro-Euro discussion evenings he had addressed recently.
